players.product: AvalonMiner bitcoin mining machines (A15 / A16 series; Avalon A1566HA hydro-cooled)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F foundry model: Canaan partners with two leading third-party foundry partners for IC fabrication, generally under three-year framework agreements that fix the production resource allocable to it before orders are placed; once an order is accepted it generally prepays at least 50% of the purchase price to secure capacity, and wafers are delivered on average four to six months after ordering. It has historically contracted with a single foundry for a specific ASIC generation. Outstanding prepayments to foundry partners were US$27.8 million at December 31, 2025 (US$10.3 million in 2024, US$37.7 million in 2023), and firm purchase obligations for foundry service were US$136,134 thousand (US$97,709 thousand at December 31, 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: prepay at least 50%; wafers in four to six months; foundry prepayments US$27.8 million; foundry purchase obligation US$136,134 thousand (end-2025)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F computing power sold in 2025: Bitcoin mining machine revenue of US$386.7 million on 35,019,343 Thash/s sold at an average US$11.0 per Thash (2024: US$212.2 million, 25,886,921 Thash/s, US$8.2), led by the A15 series at US$369.0 million, 31,995,867 Thash/s and US$11.5 per Thash; A14 series US$12.3 million, A13 US$5.3 million. Total revenues were US$529.7 million (US$269.3 million in 2024) and gross profit US$41.2 million versus gross losses of US$84.3 million in 2024 and US$240.8 million in 2023, which the company attributes mainly to higher average selling prices driven by the rise in Bitcoin price.
quarterly_data.figure: 35,019,343 Thash/s sold at US$11.0/Thash in 2025; A15 series US$369.0 million; revenue US$529.7 million; gross profit US$41.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F inventory, cryptocurrency holdings and capex: Canaan recorded inventories write-down, prepayment write-down and provision for inventory purchase commitments of US$18.6 million in 2025 (US$100.6 million in 2024, US$190.2 million in 2023); inventories were carried at US$180.8 million at December 31, 2025 (US$94.6 million in 2024). Mining cost was US$126.0 million in 2025, including US$40.6 million of depreciation; capital expenditures, primarily equipment and software, were US$24.6 million in 2025 (US$19.3 million in 2024, US$3.3 million in 2023). Cryptocurrency held was carried at fair value of US$83,339 thousand at December 31, 2025 (US$61,821 thousand at December 31, 2024). Canaan launched the Avalon Home series in 2024 and formally commercialized it in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: write-downs US$18.6 million (2025); inventories US$180.8 million; capex US$24.6 million (2025); cryptocurrency US$83,339 thousand (end-2025)
